soybean.description: India's largest oilseed crop, primarily grown in central India. Madhya Pradesh accounts for over 53% of national production. Key derivatives are soybean oil and de-oiled soy meal, which is a major protein source for poultry and aquaculture feed and a significant export commodity. Soybean cultivation transformed the agricultural economy of Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha (Maharashtra) from subsistence to commercial farming.

cotton.description: India is the world's largest producer of cotton, with cotton cultivation supporting approximately 60 million farmers and workers in the value chain. Raw cotton (kapas) is sold in mandis as seed-cotton, which is then ginned to separate lint (cotton fibre) and cottonseed. Gujarat dominates long-staple cotton production, while Vidarbha (Maharashtra) is the heartland of medium-staple cotton. Prices are significantly influenced by international cotton futures (ICE) and CCI (Cotton Corporation of India) procurement.
